3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: We were at the top floor of the business council building which had a great view of the beautiful Lachaven. I looked outside from the tall glass windows.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Tracing back the paths of the ships, I looked at the harbour. Lachaven was home to one of the largest harbours in the entire continent. Many dockyard workers were loading or unloading the containers. Work never stopped here.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: The Markian Sea stretched as far as the eye could see and it was dotted with many ships towards the horizon. They were mostly cargo ships, carrying precious goods in and out of Sordland.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: The door opened. Symon, Mikail and Edith entered the meeting room.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Symon put down his bag on the table and started collecting his documents while the others slowly took their seats.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Symon waited patiently. Once everyone was ready, he adjusted his glasses.

11.speaker: Edith Agnoc
11.text: “Mr. President. So nice to see you again.”

12.speaker: Symon Holl
12.text: “First of all, I would like to thank everyone here for their work on our tax system reform.”

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “It's great to see you all again.”

16.speaker: Symon Holl
16.text: “We all know how complicated our current system is and this work wouldn't be possible without you.”

18.speaker: Symon Holl
18.text: “Before we move ahead and start formulating a plan, we need you to determine our direction, Mr. President.”

19.speaker: Symon Holl
19.text: “We have a few possibilities as a result of the work we have done so far.”

20.speaker: Symon Holl
20.text: “We can increase, maintain or decrease the taxes for large corporations. I believe some of us in the room have a few strong opinions about this.”

21.speaker: Symon Holl
21.text: “In parallel, we can increase, maintain or decrease the taxes for small and medium businesses.”

22.speaker: Symon Holl
22.text: “The ultimate goal here is to end the recession.”

23.speaker: Symon Holl
23.text: “Let's start with the large corporations. And we'll move on to small businesses.”

24.speaker: Player
24.text: “What is the outcome if we increase the taxes for large corporations?”

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “What if we decrease the taxes for large corporations?”

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “What does everyone think we should do?”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”
27.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Question"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Increase"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Decrease"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Maintain"] == true

40.speaker: Symon Holl
40.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Question"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Increase"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Decrease"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_EnT_LargeCorpTax_Maintain"] == true) == false

44.speaker: Symon Holl
44.text: “Simply put, if we increase the taxes, we will have more government budget to spend which may come in handy. On the other hand, it's not directly helping us revitalise the economy.”

45.speaker: Symon Holl
45.text: “Our government is already in debt. This might be a way to get out of that debt.”

46.speaker: Symon Holl
46.text: “Our government budget will be hit. But in return, due to the sheer size of the economic contribution coming from these companies, it should be helpful in curbing the recession.”

47.speaker: Symon Holl
47.text: “I do think this is definitely a good option if we want to end the recession.”

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “Is there any downside to keeping the things as they are?”

52.speaker: Symon Holl
52.text: “I am of the opinion that if we don't make any changes, nothing will change. To stop the recession, we need to do something.”

53.speaker: Symon Holl
53.text: “My personal opinion is that we should decrease the taxes for large corporations. Although in short term it would cost us, in the long run it would be the most helpful option in ending the recession.”

57.speaker: Symon Holl
57.text: “We already have a budget surplus. I don't see much value in increasing our capital without investing it in possibilities that might help end the recession.”

58.speaker: Symon Holl
58.text: “However, there is one problem. The status of our budget. This might not be the greatest idea although it has its benefits. You will have to decide if it's worth the risk.”

59.speaker: Symon Holl
59.text: “Especially with the current state of our budget.”

63.speaker: Edith Agnoc
63.text: “I do believe there is one way to get out of recession. It is through the trade and the economic contribution of large corporations. Increasing their taxes will turn them on you.”

64.speaker: Mikail Aven
64.text: “I will go a step further. Increasing their taxes will have disastrous results and it will make you an enemy of them. Trust me, Mr. President. Nobody wants to make an enemy of them.”

65.speaker: Edith Agnoc
65.text: “I think this is a viable idea. Upsetting the existing balance might be less than ideal.”

66.speaker: Mikail Aven
66.text: “Me too. You would have the Group on your good side on top of solving the recession crisis, Mr. President.”

69.speaker: Edith Agnoc
69.text: “Our international trade is driven mostly by the products of these corporations. They are the backbone of our economy.”

70.speaker: Mikail Aven
70.text: “Exactly. If we let them perform better by decreasing their taxes, this should in turn lead to Sordland receiving more investment. This means more capital which means a quicker way out of the recession.”

71.speaker: Symon Holl
71.text: “Very well, Mr. President. We want to ensure the economy is on a balanced track as further destabilization might have drastic consequences.”

72.speaker: Player
72.text: “They better try to stay on *my* good side.”

73.speaker: Player
73.text: “I have to agree. Being their ally would come in handy.”

82.speaker: Player
82.text: “Decrease the taxes for large corporations.” [-4 Government Budget]

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “Increase the taxes for large corporations.” [+3 Government Budget]

87.speaker: Mikail Aven
87.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_Tax"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_Tax"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_Privatization"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_Privatization"] == false) == false)

88.speaker: Edith Agnoc
88.text: “This is going to have outrageous effects down the road.”

89.speaker: Edith Agnoc
89.text: “We won't gain anything by standing still where we are. I protest against this.”

90.speaker: Edith Agnoc
90.text: “I agree. Thanks to this, the recession will be solved in no time.”

91.speaker: Symon Holl
91.text: “Enough. The President has made his choice.”

92.speaker: Symon Holl
92.text: “I also think this was a good choice.”

93.speaker: Symon Holl
93.text: “Well then. I have taken a note of our action and I will put it to implementation as soon as possible.”

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: Symon opened his briefcase and swapped out the stack of papers he had in front with another stack.

Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_SmallMediumBusinesses"] == true) == false)

95.speaker: Symon Holl
95.text: “Let's move on to the small and medium businesses.”

99.speaker: Player
99.text: “What is the outcome if we increase the taxes for small and medium businesses?”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “What if we decrease the taxes for small and medium businesses?”

108.speaker: Symon Holl
108.text: “My personal opinion is, we should increase the taxes for small and medium corporations. It will make people angry, yes. But we can make them happier in the future *after* we end the recession.”

109.speaker: Player
109.text: “Increase the taxes for small and medium businesses.” [+2 Government Budget]

112.speaker: Symon Holl
112.text: “They are the backbone of our economy and they are comprised of mostly regular people. If we start demanding more money from them in taxes, it might cause the public to harbour ill will towards the government.”

113.speaker: Symon Holl
113.text: “It should be helpful in curbing the recession for sure. Of course that will come at the cost of losing some of our government budget.”

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “Is there any downside to keeping the things as they are?”

115.speaker: Symon Holl
115.text: “Sordland needs change to get out of recession. One way or another. I don't think we will come back on our feet by not doing anything to change our status quo.”

119.speaker: Symon Holl
119.text: “Very well. I have taken another note. We will look into how to go about implementing these changes.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “Decrease the taxes for small and medium businesses.” [-3 Government Budget]

126.speaker: Symon Holl
126.text: “On the other hand, we need to get out of debt one way or another. This can be a solution for sure.”

127.speaker: Symon Holl
127.text: “Our budget is in a good shape. I don't see the need to increase the taxes at the cost of popularity.”

132.speaker: Mikail Aven
132.text: “In the long run, increasing the taxes for small and medium businesses would make people happier with the services the government provides.”

133.speaker: Player
133.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”

137.speaker: Edith Agnoc
137.text: “I think increasing taxes for these smaller corporations is a good way to earn some extra capital so that the government can give it back to people in due time.”

138.speaker: Edith Agnoc
138.text: “People tend to be... forgetful as well.”

139.speaker: Mikail Aven
139.text: “I am with Edith and Symon on that one.”

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “Maintain the taxes for small and medium businesses.”

150.speaker: Symon Holl
150.text: “Well then... Thank you everyone. That will be all for today.”

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: They left the meeting room. I decided to stay a bit longer.

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: I went by the windows again and kept watching the sea in silence for some more time.

160.speaker: Mikail Aven
160.text: “Mr. President. Before we start, I would like to mention some rumours that I heard.”

161.speaker: Mikail Aven
161.text: “Especially the first section about the minimum wages.”

162.speaker: Mikail Aven
162.text: “Workers' Rights Act did not sit well with many business holders.”

163.speaker: Edith Agnoc
163.text: “I heard the same. This has caused these businesses to lose millions of Rens just overnight.”

165.speaker: Mikail Aven
165.text: “Mr. President. Before we start, I would like to mention some rumours that I heard.”

166.speaker: Mikail Aven
166.text: “The first section about the minimum wages would've been very damaging to many corporations.”

167.speaker: Mikail Aven
167.text: “Vetoing the recent Workers' Rights Act was welcomed by a lot of business owners.”

168.speaker: Edith Agnoc
168.text: “A good decision I'd say. Especially during a recession.”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “What is unfortunate was that this bill was enacted this late.”

171.speaker: Player
171.text: “You are in no position to question my decision.”

172.speaker: Player
172.text: “I don't care about rumours. If someone wants to say something, they can say it to me directly.”

174.speaker: Player
174.text: “I wanted to sign it but I had to make the right call.”

175.speaker: Player
175.text: “You are in no position to evaluate my decision.”

176.speaker: Player
176.text: “I don't care about rumours. If someone wants to say something, they can say it to me directly.”

264.speaker: Symon Holl
264.text: “It's not an option at this point. Our economy is in shambles.”

265.speaker: Symon Holl
265.text: “Taking what's remaining from the businesses will destroy the economy further.”

266.speaker: Player
266.text: “We could balance it by decreasing taxes of small businesses to put some relief on them.”

267.speaker: Symon Holl
267.text: “I see. I'm not sure if that's a good idea with the current state of our economy...”

270.speaker: Symon Holl
270.text: “It's not a possibility. Unless if we try and balance it with a tax decrease for small and medium businesses...”

275.speaker: Symon Holl
275.text: “It's not an option at this point. Our state is broke.”

276.speaker: Symon Holl
276.text: “We are barely functioning with the help of the taxes.”

279.speaker: Symon Holl
279.text: “I see. I'm not sure if that's a good idea with the current state of our economy...”

280.speaker: Player
280.text: “We could balance it by increasing the taxes of small businesses.”

282.speaker: Symon Holl
282.text: “It's not a possibility. Unless if we try and balance it with a tax increase for small and medium businesses...”

286.speaker: Symon Holl
286.text: “Unfortunately, that's the only thing we can do at this point anyway.”

287.speaker: Edith Agnoc
287.text: “The economy is completely destroyed, Mr. President. I don't know how we'll get out of this mess...”

291.speaker: Symon Holl
291.text: “I don't think we can do anything at this point. Although I would have preferred a decrease in taxes, it doesn't seem to be the best option.”

292.speaker: Edith Agnoc
292.text: “Our international trade is driven mostly by the products of these corporations. They are the backbone of our economy.”

293.speaker: Mikail Aven
293.text: “Exactly. An increase should be out of the question. These companies are the backbone of our economy and our way out of the recession.”

303.speaker: Symon Holl
303.text: “We will be giving people some relief by enacting tax breaks for small and medium businesses. And there will be an increase for large corporation taxes, which will help us sustain our balance."

304.speaker: Player
304.text: “We'll increase the taxes for large corporations and balance it with a decrease for small businesses.”

305.speaker: Player
305.text: “We'll decrease the taxes for large corporations and balance the budget with an increase for smaller businesses.” [-2 Government Budget]
